cancer_indication: ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer after progression on at least one line of endocrine therapy including prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure
moa: Elacestrant is an oral, non-steroidal SERD that binds estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1/ERα), acts as a high-affinity antagonist, and promotes ubiquitin–proteasome–mediated degradation of ER in ER-positive breast-cancer cells. This reduces ER protein levels and estrogen-responsive transcriptional programs that drive proliferation and survival in luminal (HR+/HER2–) disease, including tumors with activating ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations that emerge under aromatase inhibitor therapy. In preclinical ER+ models, including endocrine-resistant and CDK4/6 inhibitor–resistant patient-derived xenografts, elacestrant suppresses estrogen-response gene sets, downregulates cell-cycle effectors, induces cell-cycle arrest, and maintains antitumor activity where ER signaling remains a key dependency.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.description: Gene set representing estrogen-response transcriptional programs regulated by ERα in hormone-responsive breast-cancer cells.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.interpretation: In ER+/HER2– breast cancer, these early estrogen-response genes capture ER-dependent signaling that underlies luminal tumor proliferation; elacestrant antagonizes and degrades ERα, leading to broad suppression of these signatures in responsive and ESR1-mutated models.

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_NUCLEAR_INITIATED.description: KEGG-based nuclear estrogen signaling pathway encompassing ER-mediated regulation of gene expression in response to estrogen.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_NUCLEAR_INITIATED.interpretation: ER-driven estrogen signaling supports growth and survival of luminal ER+/HER2– tumors and often remains active in ESR1-mutated disease after aromatase inhibitors; elacestrant targets this nuclear ER signaling axis by degrading ERα and reducing estrogen-dependent transcription.

WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING.description: Estrogen signaling pathway centered on ERα-dependent regulation of estrogen-responsive gene expression.
WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING.interpretation: This pathway reflects the broader ER-regulated transcriptional network in ER+/HER2– breast cancer; its persistent activity, particularly in tumors with ESR1 mutations, marks continued ER dependence that can be disrupted by elacestrant-mediated ER degradation.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.description: Gene set capturing late estrogen-response genes regulated downstream of sustained ERα activity.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.interpretation: Late estrogen-response signatures form part of the extended ER transcriptional program maintaining luminal identity and proliferation in ER+ disease; endocrine-relapsed tumors often show reduced activity of these gene sets, whereas elacestrant-responsive tumors exhibit marked on-treatment downregulation.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Gene set of E2F transcription factor targets involved in G1–S transition, DNA replication, and cell-cycle progression.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: In ER+/HER2– breast cancer, ER signaling promotes cyclin D–CDK4/6 and E2F-regulated cell-cycle programs; elacestrant downregulates key cell-cycle proteins and suppresses E2F-target gene expression in CDK4/6 inhibitor–resistant models, contributing to cell-cycle arrest.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Gene set comprising regulators of the G2/M checkpoint and mitotic entry within the cell cycle.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: Hyperactive G2/M checkpoint and cell-cycle gene sets support uncontrolled proliferation in ER+ tumors; elacestrant-induced ER blockade is associated with suppression of G2/M and broader cell-cycle signatures and with growth inhibition in ER+ and CDK4/6 inhibitor–resistant models.

HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.description: Gene set associated with mTORC1 pathway activation as part of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling network.
HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activation is described as a canonical driver of endocrine resistance in ER+ breast cancer via ER-independent survival signaling; preclinical work combining elacestrant with mTOR inhibition (e.g., everolimus) shows enhanced antitumor activity, highlighting this pathway as an important resistance and combination target context.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Gene set summarizing activity of the PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling axis in tumor cells.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling is frequently altered in endocrine-resistant ER+ metastatic breast cancer and provides ER-independent survival signals; combination studies of elacestrant with PI3K or mTOR inhibitors and class-level endocrine-resistance data underscore the relevance of this pathway for both resistance biology and rational combinations.

KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: KEGG ErbB signaling pathway involving HER family receptors (e.g., HER2/ERBB2, EGFR) and their downstream cascades.
KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Endocrine-resistant ER+ breast cancers often show increased RTK/ERBB activity and HER2-enriched transcriptomic features, with reduced benefit from ER-targeted therapy; such RTK/ErbB signaling shifts are discussed as escape routes from ER dependence that may limit the impact of ER degradation by elacestrant when they dominate tumor biology.

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Gene set including core mediators and regulators of programmed cell death pathways.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: ER blockade via SERDs, including elacestrant, is associated with engagement of apoptotic machinery in ER-dependent models and tumor regression; endocrine-resistant states often show diminished pro-apoptotic signaling, indicating that effective activation of apoptosis downstream of ER and cell-cycle inhibition is an important determinant of treatment response.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Activating ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations (for example Y537S and D538G) maintain high ER transcriptional activity and strong estrogen-response signatures under estrogen deprivation; in the phase III EMERALD trial, tumors with ESR1 mutations derived greater progression-free survival benefit from elacestrant than ESR1 wild-type disease, and ESR1-mutated, endocrine-resistant patient-derived xenografts showed marked suppression of estrogen-response programs and tumor growth on elacestrant, supporting mutant ERα signaling as a sensitivity-associated state.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Endocrine-relapsed ER+ breast cancers frequently show downregulation of early and late estrogen-response gene sets and may exhibit ER loss or marked ER downregulation, which is described as a mechanism of resistance to SERMs and SERDs; the deep-research output notes that elacestrant requires ERα for binding and degradation and that tumors evolving ER loss or very low estrogen-response activity are intrinsically resistant, implying that reduced ESR1 expression and signaling confers resistance to elacestrant.

notes: JSON fields are derived directly from the provided deep-research output for elacestrant in human ER+/HER2– breast cancer; ESR1 is the only gene with explicit, repeated gene-level sensitivity and resistance associations, while PI3K/AKT/mTOR and ERBB/RTK pathways are treated at the pathway/class level rather than as individual gene biomarkers. Most adaptive resistance and combination insights (e.g., with PI3K, mTOR, and CDK4/6 inhibitors) are supported by preclinical endocrine-resistance literature and early clinical data and should be interpreted in that context.
